old_first: A position can finish inside its limit after exceeding that limit during the intervening period, as Figure~\ref{fig:example} illustrates
new_first: Dealer position limits concern the largest exposure reached before a review horizon ends
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: A position can finish inside its limit after exceeding that limit during the intervening period, as Figure~\ref{fig:example} illustrates. For a market maker, the relevant forecast therefore concerns the largest exposure before the next review, rather than the endpoint alone. The distinction changes the response variable, the observations available for training, and the interpretation of successful prediction. We study how established historical and conditional forecasts perform when every method targets this same sampled absolute-position peak.
new: Dealer position limits concern the largest exposure reached before a review horizon ends. A position can finish within its limit after crossing it earlier (Figure~\ref{fig:example}). We compare historical and conditional forecasts of this sampled absolute-position peak.

old_first: Simple historical rules provide a demanding reference because they already incorporate information about the current position and its recent path behavior
new_first: Historical headroom already combines the current position with completed past peak behavior
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: Simple historical rules provide a demanding reference because they already incorporate information about the current position and its recent path behavior. A conditional model must improve on that information while estimating additional relationships from a finite, changing sequence of completed outcomes. More predictors can help distinguish current conditions, but they also increase sensitivity to the historical sample and the strength of regularization. We examine these competing effects through matched histories, alternative reference rules, and repeated chronological comparisons.
new: Historical headroom already combines the current position with completed past peak behavior. Conditional models estimate additional relationships from finite historical windows. Matched histories and update schedules show whether the added conditioning improves the forecast.

old_first: Our empirical comparison joins an hourly FX market-maker record with weekly U.S
new_first: Our comparisons cover hourly FX positions and weekly U.S
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: Our empirical comparison joins an hourly FX market-maker record with weekly U.S. primary-dealer position-category aggregates, using a common forecasting objective. The methods predict source-native peaks separately for each series, so monetary magnitudes from different reporting systems remain separate throughout evaluation. We compare regression, local quantiles, historical rules, and additional conditional benchmarks on the same completed response within each comparison. The evidence asks where added conditioning helps, whether that advantage survives a change of reference, and how scores relate to breaches.
new: Our comparisons cover hourly FX positions and weekly U.S. primary-dealer aggregates. Each series retains source-native units and its own evaluation grid. Two pre-specified comparisons anchor the analysis. They compare long-history FX regression with a shorter rolling rule, and Treasury regression with matched historical headroom.

old_first: The clearest repeated gains arise for long-history FX regression at the shorter forecast horizon, rather than across every conditional specification
new_first: [consolidated]
note: Duplicate finding paragraph merged into First/Third contributions and Section7; all results remain in tables/Supplement.
old: The clearest repeated gains arise for long-history FX regression at the shorter forecast horizon, rather than across every conditional specification. Against a historical headroom rule with the same history, its later-period loss changes by -14.77\%. The earlier-period matched comparison changes loss by -16.62\%, and the evaluated coverage correction preserves the later advantage. Changing the comparison to the shorter-history rolling reference reverses the direction of the earlier-period result, while weekly comparisons frequently favor historical rules.

new_first: [consolidated]
note: Duplicate finding paragraph merged into First/Third contributions and Section7; all results remain in tables/Supplement.
old: A lower quantile score also leaves a separate operational question about how often the predicted limit is crossed during the forecast period. Elementary-score curves and error-weight comparisons show why these assessments can disagree, with the relevant comparison stated explicitly in each case. For managers setting monitoring limits, the practical implication is to evaluate prediction errors and exceedance frequency together before selecting a more complex forecast.

old_first: Net-position forecasting already has a close empirical lineage in the market-making literature, where Wisniewski and colleagues predict signed next-hour endpoint intervals
new_first: Wisniewski and colleagues forecast signed next-hour position intervals using historical states, calendar information and local prediction methods \citep{wisniewski2020,wisniewski2024}
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: Net-position forecasting already has a close empirical lineage in the market-making literature, where Wisniewski and colleagues predict signed next-hour endpoint intervals. Their methods combine historical positions, calendar information, neighboring observations, and normalized prediction intervals, with sequential training, calibration, and evaluation \citep{wisniewski2020,wisniewski2024}. They also report scores and coverage tests together, providing a direct precedent for the joint evaluation of interval forecasts. Our response instead requires the complete future path segment and includes the current absolute position as a known lower bound. This distinction creates different training labels and different limits, even when the numerical forecasting engine follows the same broad family.
new: Wisniewski and colleagues forecast signed next-hour position intervals using historical states, calendar information and local prediction methods \citep{wisniewski2020,wisniewski2024}. Their chronological training, calibration and test design reports scores and coverage together. The present peak response uses a complete future path segment and the current magnitude, producing different labels and limits.

old_first: Financial path-risk studies establish that a within-period extreme can matter more than the value observed at the end of the period
new_first: Path-risk forecasts address within-period extremes
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: Financial path-risk studies establish that a within-period extreme can matter more than the value observed at the end of the period. MaxVaR evaluates the worst cumulative portfolio return under a fixed portfolio and diffusion assumptions, including a conversion from endpoint probabilities to path risk \citep{boudoukh2004}. The payment-liquidity thesis studies conditional maximum deficits using a different path-risk target and confidential transactions \citep{hoogen2017}. Related settlement studies examine tail liquidity needs and collateral requirements in their respective payment systems \citep{petrunia2019,arjani2020}. Duffie and colleagues analyze dealer capacity and Treasury-market functioning, with additional out-of-sample PnL quantile comparisons in their appendix \citep{duffie2023}. Our empirical contribution concerns matched forecasts of the present peak-position target across the FX record and related public position aggregates.
new: Path-risk forecasts address within-period extremes. MaxVaR studies the worst cumulative portfolio return under fixed holdings and diffusion assumptions \citep{boudoukh2004}. The payment-liquidity thesis forecasts conditional maximum deficits from confidential transactions \citep{hoogen2017}. Settlement studies examine tail liquidity needs and collateral requirements \citep{petrunia2019,arjani2020}. Duffie and colleagues study dealer capacity and Treasury-market functioning, including PnL quantile forecasts \citep{duffie2023}. These responses differ from the sampled absolute-position peak.

old_first: Quantile estimation and evaluation supply established tools for comparing conditional peak forecasts against historical rules on a shared response
new_first: Regression quantiles target asymmetric forecast errors directly \citep{koenker1978}
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: Quantile estimation and evaluation supply established tools for comparing conditional peak forecasts against historical rules on a shared response. Regression quantiles directly target asymmetric forecast errors through the associated loss function, providing the basic statistical building block \citep{koenker1978}. Conditional autoregressive quantiles and quantile forests provide additional conditioning structures for different forecasting applications \citep{engle2004,meinshausen2006}. Consistent scoring rules and elementary-score representations explain why rankings can vary across distinct evaluation questions \citep{gneiting2011,ehm2016}. We connect these tools to mature path labels, matched historical controls, and the stability of observed score and breach differences. The positioning in Table~\ref{tab:literature} locates the substantive comparison in the peak response, completed labels and explicitly matched reference rules.
new: Regression quantiles target asymmetric forecast errors directly \citep{koenker1978}. Autoregressive quantiles and quantile forests supply other conditioning structures \citep{engle2004,meinshausen2006}. Consistent scores and elementary-score representations permit comparison across evaluation preferences \citep{gneiting2011,ehm2016}. Table~\ref{tab:literature} locates the present peak response, completed labels and matched historical controls.

The historical-peak rule uses completed absolute peaks directly, and the endpoint-derived rule adds an empirical absolute-displacement quantile to the observed floor. old_first: Conditional quantile regression links completed peak headroom to issue-known position histories and calendar information, using training-based transformations and ridge regularization
new_first: Ridge quantile regression links mature headroom to issue-known position states and calendar variables
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: Conditional quantile regression links completed peak headroom to issue-known position histories and calendar information, using training-based transformations and ridge regularization. The original predictor set contains 33 features before its intercept, with all transformations fitted inside the chronological training sample. The parsimonious variant concentrates on a smaller state description, while the expanded ridge comparison changes the penalty menu with the richer predictor set held fixed. These comparisons distinguish changes in the conditioning information from changes in the strength of regularization rather than attributing every gain to feature reduction.
new: Ridge quantile regression links mature headroom to issue-known position states and calendar variables. The larger set contains 33 predictors plus an unpenalized intercept. The four-predictor variant uses current magnitude, signed level and two increment RMS measures. All standardization uses mature training observations. Expanded-menu regression changes only the penalty grid.

old_first: Local quantile methods condition on neighboring historical states, with a scale-adjusted variant using training information to normalize the comparison
new_first: Local quantiles use neighboring historical states, with an increment-scaled variant
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: Local quantile methods condition on neighboring historical states, with a scale-adjusted variant using training information to normalize the comparison. The filtered-path benchmark recursively simulates signed positions using GARCH-standardized empirical innovations drawn independently with replacement \citep{hull1998,barone1999}. The other benchmarks estimate a quantile from response distributions in tree leaves or fit tails of volatility-scaled peak headroom \citep{meinshausen2006,mcneilfrey2000}. These are the existing fitted specifications, with every complete result and numerical or structural failure documented in the Supplement. Their different conditioning assumptions make the actual executed procedure, rather than its family name alone, the relevant object for comparison.
new: Local quantiles use neighboring historical states, with an increment-scaled variant. Filtered paths simulate positions from GARCH-standardized empirical innovations drawn independently with replacement \citep{hull1998,barone1999}. Quantile forests use leaf distributions; tail methods fit volatility-scaled headroom \citep{meinshausen2006,mcneilfrey2000}. The Supplement lists all complete results and numerical or structural failures.

old_first: The further robustness comparisons address calibration, forecast combination, and conservative selection while keeping the peak response and chronological information restrictions explicit
new_first: Additional comparisons apply delayed calibration, fixed combinations and conservative selection to the same peak response
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: The further robustness comparisons address calibration, forecast combination, and conservative selection while keeping the peak response and chronological information restrictions explicit. A headroom version of the symmetric absolute-value quantile recursion follows the CAViaR family, and finite delayed calibration wrappers update only after outcomes mature \citep{engle2004,gibbs2021}. Fixed mean and median combinations aggregate the specified forecasts, while a paired-difference one-standard-error rule favors simpler reports within its stated validation tolerance. Every method earns its comparison against the historical headroom rule through its actual score and breach outcomes on the shared evaluation origins.
new: Additional comparisons apply delayed calibration, fixed combinations and conservative selection to the same peak response. A headroom CAViaR recursion and calibration wrappers follow existing methods \citep{engle2004,gibbs2021}. Calibration parameters update after outcomes mature. Fixed mean and median combinations use predefined members; the one-standard-error rule favors stronger shrinkage within a paired validation-loss tolerance.

Predictors use issue-known observations, and training-only transformations remain fixed until the next scheduled refit rather than learning from future evaluation outcomes. Parameter selection uses the preceding validation segment, after which the evaluation proceeds on the complete specified issue grid.
new: At refit \(r\), training labels are eligible only when \(i+H\le r\). Predictors use issue-known observations, and training transforms remain fixed until the next refit. The preceding validation segment selects parameters; the entire specified evaluation grid then receives forecasts.

old_first: The weekly data are signed position-category aggregates, so offsetting exposures across dealers can reduce the aggregate while individual gross exposures remain large
new_first: The weekly categories share a reporting system and economic components, so related series are not independent dealer replications
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: The weekly data are signed position-category aggregates, so offsetting exposures across dealers can reduce the aggregate while individual gross exposures remain large. Related categories share a reporting system and economic components, which limits an interpretation of their comparisons as independent replications across institutions. The downloaded economic-date series also differs from a reconstruction of the observations available at each historical publication time. The sampled target measures recorded positions; excursions between observations, settlement cash needs, and the costs of actual limit decisions require additional measurement.
new: The weekly categories share a reporting system and economic components, so related series are not independent dealer replications. Treasury comparisons replay the downloaded economic-date vintage; historical publication-time information is not reconstructed. Aggregation can offset gross dealer exposure, and between-observation excursions remain unmeasured.

old_first: The later analyses and working-reference tests describe the observed records after earlier results had informed the research process and additional comparisons
new_first: Causal and individual-predictor effects are outside this design
note: Rewritten with direct subject, active construction and shorter sentences.
old: The later analyses and working-reference tests describe the observed records after earlier results had informed the research process and additional comparisons. Their p-values therefore do not account for the full sequence of model, sample, diagnostic, and presentation choices made during that process. The finite calibration wrapper, empirical endpoint rule, and dependent financial paths also require distinctions from the population assumptions in Proposition~\ref{prop:levy}. The main evidence supports a bounded comparative forecasting result, with external validity, prospective calibration, and economic decision value remaining questions for future evaluation. The score uses a nineteen-to-one error-weight ratio for evaluation, which does not measure the actual costs of a limit decision.
new: Causal and individual-predictor effects are outside this design. The financial procedures provide no coverage guarantee under their dependence and calibration scheme. Trading and funding gains are not measured, and scoring weights do not identify actual decision costs. The calibrated simulations leave the hourly mechanism unresolved and fail to reproduce persistent weekly losses. Their DGPs bundle frequency, validation length and volatility laws.
